A boss fight. Attacks are lists of steps: A boss fight. Attacks are lists of steps (warn, dash, jump with a shockwave, shoot rings/fans/aimed bullets, summon minions, become invulnerable…). Phases pick which attacks it uses — the next phase starts when its health drops to a percentage — and a death sequence plays when it is defeated. Give it Health (Disappear, with its own variable like bossHP) and a Damager for contact damage. Build it with 🧩 Advanced Scratch or ask the AI.
A clickable button. On click it runs an: A clickable button. On click it runs an effect: goscene (change scene), setvar, addvar, say, save or load. Put it on a UI layer; add a Label for its text. Great for menus and HUD.

A custom behavior written as a tiny rule: A custom behavior written as a tiny rule script (when → do). Usually created by the AI when the request is too complex for the other behaviors.
A day/night cycle. Add it to one object: A day/night cycle. Add it to one object (a controller, can be invisible). It dims the scene at night and brightens it by day, and sets the variables isDay/isNight/timeOfDay you can read in the AI or in blocks (e.g. spawn certain enemies only at night). In Platformer mode, adding it creates a 'Sky' layer under all the others with a Sun and a Moon already linked (Top-down has no sky — just the light changes) — give them your own sprites there. The sky is drawn behind everything (tilemaps, trees, player), fixed to the screen; the sun and moon cross it and leave the screen completely before day/night changes. Put clouds or stars in the Sky layer too. Platformer: turn on 'coverDark' and it also gets darker the more solid blocks are above the player (caves, underground) — torches still light it up; it sets the variables cover (0 to 1) and underground (0 or 1). 'True black darkness' makes the dark pure black (no night tint) and fully dark underground. Lighting style: Smooth = soft circles of light; Blocks = light computed block by block (each Light then chooses whether solid blocks stop it, whether it colours what it touches and whether it adds up with other lights). Works for Top-down and Platformer.
A grid of tiles you paint in the editor: A grid of tiles you paint in the editor (ground, walls, level geometry). Solid tiles become collision automatically. Add it to an empty object, then paint with the Tiles panel. Turn on 'Breakable' to let individual tiles be destroyed (by bullets, melee, damagers, stomping, touching, or the 'Break a tile' block).
A hotbar. Scroll the mouse wheel (or pre: A hotbar. Scroll the mouse wheel (or press 1-9) to pick a slot. List the slots in 'items' as name:#color, comma-separated (e.g. pickaxe:#8B5A2B,axe:#B0B0B0,sword:#AEE1FF). ANY name is an item — make your own (shovel, hammer, magic wand…) with the '＋ New item' button, or add ':look' to a slot: a built-in drawing (pickaxe, axe, sword, shovel, hammer, hoe, tile) or a picture file (e.g. wand:#FFFFFF:Assets/sprites/wand.png). A Harvestable whose 'tool' is that name only accepts it. You OWN a slot once you have item:<name> (give it with 'Give an item' / buying). The selected owned slot sets holding:<name>=1 — use that as a tilemap's 'requires' so only the right tool mines it. The held tool is drawn in the player's hand.
